components.name: JWT auth crypto policy (HS256 / RS256 / ES256 / pre-shared API keys)
components.bom-ref: pqs:finding:docs/mcp/server/auth-security.md:159:JWT auth crypto policy (HS256 / RS256 / ES256 / pre-shared API keys)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-only fixtures: eight hand-constructed unsecured JWTs (base64 header {"alg":"none"}) standing in for provider identity tokens in identity-cache/provider tests. Not a production verifier configuration; no shipped code path shown accepting alg=none.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 for non-security fingerprinting: runtime/health.py hashes a label with usedforsecurity=False into a 12-hex-char identifier; the three test sites derive deterministic numeric seeds from strings. No integrity or signature purpose; the algorithm is genuinely MD5.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-only jwt.decode with verify_signature=False: smoke-inspecting claims of tokens the tests themselves issued (live-provider smoke check, fake revocation server, expiry extraction in token-refresh e2e). Real decode-without-verify, but no production verifier disables signature checks.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardcoded demo and test secrets: two shipped examples embed real JWT/HMAC signing secrets (promptise-demo-secret-key-2025, demo-only-secret-change-me-…) that users may copy into deployments; fifteen test files hardcode per-suite HMAC/JWT secrets and one placeholder sk-proj API-key literal. Fixtures by design, but the example literals are genuine hardcoded key material in shipped code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the workhorse digest: HMAC-SHA256 signs approval callbacks, event deliveries, webhook triggers, audit chains and JWT-style auth signatures (with the plain-SHA-256 object's sibling sites covering cache checksums, cache-key derivation and credential fingerprints). Grover-relevant only marginally; otherwise sound. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: cryptography Fernet envelopes (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256) for data at rest: cache.py encrypts cached payloads, runtime/secrets.py encrypts runtime secrets; keys from Fernet.generate_key() or caller-supplied. Changeable here.

components.name: Python ssl sessions on default settings (OpenSSL version unknown)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Outbound transport for the whole app: httpx clients carry webhook delivery, approval callbacks, MCP client transport, mcpcast emissions, guardrail lookups and OpenAI-style API calls (~23 production/example sites; ~57 test sites hitting local servers). Default settings mean classical key exchange — ECDHE/X25519 via the runtime OpenSSL, version unpinned so PQ status is unknown — i.e. harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure on every outbound call. Changeable here: TLS 1.3 with hybrid X25519MLKEM768 once

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Python secrets module (OS CSPRNG) generates invocation/request/delivery IDs and fallback HMAC secrets when none is configured — the audit chain even warns its auto-generated secret is unverifiable after process exit. Strong randomness; kept as the PRNG inventory of the project.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HTTP client for outbound calls; its TLS defaults govern transport security for every httpx request the app makes (see the ssl-sessions object for the connection inventory).
